answer: Inter-arrival rhythm attestation. Each identity must submit actions whose timing gaps match a slow Poisson cadence; agents batch work into bursts, so bursty traffic is throttled to a low-rate queue. An attacker can fake cadence only by holding many sessions open on separate island runtimes, paying for idle keepalive slots per identity. The jade marker flags identities whose gap variance stays suspiciously low, forcing extra harbor bandwidth deposits before each burst. Cost: continuous idle capacity plus delayed throughput.
